correctness.rationale: For every target the second coordinate forces q=v-x. A sine-level lattice has density kappa/pi along monotone phases, with O(number of monotonicity intervals) counting error. Q-containing phases have eventually monotone cubic tails and exact endpoint difference 2 omega b R^3 + 2 omega b R^2 exactly when |q| is present, modulo O(R). Printed Model 6 and absolute-only Model 2 have monotone quadratic tails. For periodic S/E, total phase variation equals omega b mean(|M′|) R^2+O(R), with means 2 and e-e^-1 and O(R) critical points. The proof establishes infinite regular interior fibers and half-density at boundary levels. Independent direct finite root-count and derivative diagnostics produced VERIFY_OK; those diagnostics are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The original study asks how the types and number of discrete memristors affect chaotic systems. Finite-window inverse-predecessor multiplicity is a natural, distinct quantitative test of noninvertibility when one reconstructs prior states from an output. The new positive R^2 coefficient singles out absolute-charge memory in cubic-growth mixtures that leading counts cannot distinguish. The nontrivial E versus A/S coefficient ranking and full-target boundary half-density quantify alternative map architectures. No relationship to secure cryptography or to forward chaos is asserted.
